quote: Beweise, dass durch die Theilung der Abel'schen Functionen alle Körper ge- funden werden können, welche in Bezug auf einen algebraischen Functionenkörper relativ Abel'sch sind.
english: Prove that, by the division of Abelian functions, all fields can be found which are relatively Abelian with respect to an algebraic function field.
topic: Three research notes: simultaneous rational approximation of (1-z)^α and (1-z)^{-α} as a route to proving 2^√2 irrational; obtaining all relatively Abelian fields over an algebraic function field by division of Abelian functions; and a claim, with the start of a proof, that every small region of a Riemann surface contains points whose product as prime ideals lies in a given class.

triage.modern_statement: Let K be an algebraic function field in one variable, i.e. the function field of a compact Riemann surface or of a smooth projective curve X. Show that every abelian extension L/K can be generated by values or coordinates of division points (torsion points) of Abelian functions. In modern terms, every abelian covering of X should come from pulling back an isogeny of the Jacobian of X along the Abel–Jacobi map. For ramified coverings, this needs a generalized Jacobian of X with respect to a modulus. This is the function-field analogue of Kronecker's Jugendtraum and of Hilbert's 12th problem (explicit construction of abelian extensions).
triage.answered_by: Over an algebraically closed constant field this is geometric class field theory. It was developed by M. Rosenlicht (1954, 1957) and S. Lang (1956) and set out in J.-P. Serre's 'Groupes algébriques et corps de classes' (1959). They showed that every abelian covering of a smooth projective curve comes from an étale isogeny onto a generalized Jacobian (the ordinary Jacobian in the unramified case). The variant over finite constant fields, where explicit class field theory works through Drinfeld modules, was developed by Drinfeld and Hayes in the 1970s. That variant comes from my background knowledge; the search did not confirm the attribution.

evidence.claim: Geometric class field theory, pioneered by Lang and Rosenlicht in the 1950s and expounded in Serre's 1959 book, describes the abelian covers of a smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field through étale isogenies onto its generalized Jacobians. In the unramified case the ordinary Jacobian is enough.

Geometric class field theory describes the abelian coverings of a curve geometrically through generalized Jacobian varieties: connected abelian coverings come from isogenies onto the generalized Jacobian for a modulus m. This holds over any perfect constant field.
Over function fields with finite constant field, explicit class field theory via Drinfeld modules solves a case of Hilbert's 12th problem, for example by constructing the narrow Hilbert class field.

triage.why: The note asks whether all abelian extensions of an algebraic function field can be produced by dividing Abelian functions, meaning torsion of the Jacobian. Geometric class field theory (Rosenlicht, Lang, Serre, 1950s) answers yes, provided generalized Jacobians are used for the ramified case. Plain Jacobian division covers only the unramified extensions, so Hilbert's wording is exactly right only in that case. The note is not itself one of the 23 problems, but it is closely related to the 12th (explicit abelian extensions). Work on geometric class field theory and on the function-field versions of the 12th problem is still going on: the sources include a 2019 paper and a 2025 preprint. My confidence is medium because I am matching the note to this theory by its content; no source discusses this particular diary entry.
